title: Switchboard and Connect are the same Reactor with different outward surfaces
content:
## One engine, two faces

Switchboard runs the same Reactor library as Connect — on a Node server instead of in a browser. It loads the same packages, the same document models, the same reducers. The only thing that differs is what each host turns outward:

- **Connect** renders editors. It gives *people* a UI.
- **Switchboard** exposes GraphQL and MCP endpoints. It gives *code* an API.

Because both hosts run the same engine over the same operation log, writes converge without a reconciliation layer. An operation authored in Connect arrives in Switchboard through sync; a mutation dispatched over GraphQL shows up in Connect. There is no "API model" separate from the "UI model" — there is one document model, and two ways to reach it.

Switchboard serves both protocols at once:

- **GraphQL** — composed from subgraphs, one per installed package. Web apps, mobile clients, and integrations query documents and dispatch actions here.
- **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) — the same Reactor surfaced as tools an AI agent can call.

Locally, `ph vetra` starts a Switchboard alongside Connect, hot-reloading subgraphs as you edit them:

```bash
ph vetra
# Reactor booted
# Subgraphs composed — GraphQL at http://localhost:4001/graphql
# MCP at http://localhost:4001/mcp
```

In production Switchboard ships as a Docker container with a persistent Reactor store, and scales out behind a load balancer.

## The design consequence

Choosing between Connect and Switchboard is never a data-modelling decision — it is a question of who the consumer is. Browser drag-and-drop belongs in Connect, because Switchboard has no UI layer. A query endpoint for a mobile client belongs in a Switchboard subgraph, because Connect is not an API. Neither choice touches the document model.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/06-switchboard/01-what-is-switchboard.mdx (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Connect renders editors for people; Switchboard exposes GraphQL and MCP for code. Both host the same Reactor and the same document models, so writes on either side converge.
